accuracy.evidence: Matches the DfE Relationships Education statutory guidance (honesty, truthfulness, sharing, permission-seeking and respecting others' belongings) and KS1 PSHE Association themes on right and wrong and fairness. Fair shares uses 6 strawberries over 3 plates, so 2 each is exact; the cup tale models telling the truth after an accident, not punishment.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the known early-years errors: judging wrongness by the size of the damage rather than the intention (cup tale), 'a lie is fine if no one finds out' (locked prediction and challenge tags hide and seen), finders keepers (park toy prediction), and 'I found it so I get more' (strawberries prediction and the 'found' tag).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagright combines tappable picture tales with trust hearts that drop or rise by choice, a two-box drag sort of six belongings into Ask first or Mine to use, a plate-by-plate fair-share deal with an Is it fair? check, and an uphill hard-but-right path. No other flag lab models trust as a state; the 6-token shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Children see consequences rather than read rules: hiding the cup makes the trust hearts fall when Mum finds out, telling keeps them, blaming the cat hurts two characters. Strawberries only pass the fairness check when each plate holds the same number, so 'fair means the same' is discovered by counting, not told.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions before acting: what happens if Zara hides the broken cup, whether a toy car found in the park is now yours, and whether keeping 4 of 6 strawberries is fair. Each is tested straight away by the tale, the sort or the share that follows.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with three answers each and ten tagged wrong-answer messages (hide, blame, grab, sneak, more, found, seen, share, laugh, ignore). Each names why the choice hurts someone and what the kind or honest choice is, in words a five-year-old can follow.

readability.evidence: Family audience: kid text FK 1.5 against the 5.0 target and adult text FK 5.7 against 10.0, measured by the validator. Words are short and concrete (truth, ask first, fair, share, kind), and the key PSHE terms honesty, permission and fairness are used in the adult notes.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean and explanation overlap under 12 percent. Kid paragraphs each add one idea (feelings, telling the truth, asking before taking, fair shares); adult paragraphs give the curriculum link, named mistakes, the home conversation idea and what each lab step shows.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light for every step: the tale pictures and trust hearts fill the width, sort boxes sit side by side with large tap targets, the three plates fit in one row, and buttons wrap. walk.cjs passes on desktop and iPhone 13 with Show me finishing each task.

accessibility.evidence: axe reports no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme. Every drag has a tap-then-tap or button route, the young-learner class enlarges hit areas, the canvas has an aria-label, and a live region reads each tale outcome and heart count so nothing relies on colour or animation alone.

sources: DfE (2019) Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education statutory guidance (Families and people who care for me; Caring friendships; Respectful relationships)
PSHE Association (2020) Programme of Study for PSHE Education, Key Stage 1: Relationships and Living in the Wider World
Piaget (1932) The Moral Judgment of the Child: young children judge by consequence rather than intention
Kohlberg stages and early-years research on fairness and equal sharing (Fehr, Bernhard and Rockenbach 2008, Nature)
